newsitem.title: USA: U.S. trade gap seen edging higher in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trade gap seen edging higher in June.

text.p: The U.S. trade gap is expected to have widened only modestly in June, causing little concern among market analysts despite persistent official U.S. saber-rattling over Japan's bulging trade surplus.
A healthy economy in the United States and feeble growth among its trading partners continue to balloon imports well in excess of export growth, analysts said.
"U.S. domestic demand in particular versus Europe or Japan justifies a wider trade deficit than we saw in May," said Suzanne Rizzo, domestic economist at MFR Inc.

The Commerce Department will release its June trade report at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Wednesday. The consensus forecast of a Reuters economist poll is for a widening to $10.36 billion from $10.23 bilion in May.
Imports appear to have climbed in June, judging from a sharp increase in wholesale inventories that month, especially in the auto sector, analysts said.
"That was a very large increase in June wholesale inventories, which are often a depository for imports. So that suggests we may have gotten a large increase on the import side," said Rizzo.
Stocks of unsold goods piled up on wholesalers' shelves in June at the fastest pace since the 1982 recession, rising 1.9 percent, while new car inventories surged 5.1 percent.

Because domestically produced vehicles are shipped directly to dealers from manufacturers, they do not show up in wholesale inventories, suggesting a large boost in auto imports in June, analysts said.
But barring a surprisingly sharp move either up or down, the trade report was seen having little impact on the Treasury market or the dollar.

"There's a small risk that we'll get a little more imports than we're expecting, but I don't think we'll get a significant shift," said Dan Seto, senior economist at Nikko Securities Co International Inc, who sees a June deficit of $10 billion.

The trade report comes two days after Japan released its own customs-cleared trade data for July, which showed its surplus with the United States at 849 billion yen, up 35.7 percent on a year-over-year basis.
U.S. officials have repeatedly expressed concern over Japan's trade bulge.
Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang told Reuters in Tokyo on Monday, "we are concerned," about the trade figures.
